Also confirm that the response does not collapse item status into the parent order status and that unrelated customers' items are excluded.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the customer who owns the order-item history being queried.

functions.name: test_api_customer_order_items_list_own_history

scenario.draft: Verify that the customer order-item list supports business filtering and sorting across order context, item status, creation time, and variant scope. Prepare a customer's order history containing items across multiple statuses and dates, then query with combinations such as status, orderId or orderNumber, productVariantId, createdAtFrom/createdAtTo, and explicit sort values. Confirm the returned page contains only matching items, respects the requested ordering, and still returns the correct pagination metadata. The scenario should also verify that the endpoint remains a browsing view only: it should surface summaries and timestamps for matching items, not expanded snapshots or unrelated child collections.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the customer whose items will be filtered and browsed.

functions.name: test_api_customer_order_items_filtered_browse

scenario.draft: Verify that the endpoint behaves correctly when the customer's accessible order-item set is empty or narrowed by filters to no matches. After authenticating, request the list using a filter combination that does not match any of the customer's items, and confirm the API returns an empty page with pagination metadata reflecting zero records and zero pages rather than an error. This protects the business expectation that list browsing is resilient when there are no qualifying order items and still respects customer ownership boundaries.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the customer who is performing the browse request.

functions.name: test_api_customer_order_items_empty_result_page

scenario.draft: Test the happy path where an authenticated customer creates a purchased order item for a real order they own and a purchasable variant that exists under a seller-owned product. Verify the response contains the persisted order item with the correct order reference, variant reference, quantity, and server-managed paid lifecycle state, while null lifecycle timestamps remain unset at creation. Also verify that the operation uses the customer session as the actor boundary and that the created item is linked to the customer's order history rather than any catalog-only resource. As a business edge, confirm that the same variant added again in the same order is treated as a quantity merge into one order item rather than a duplicate line, preserving the one-order-item-per-variant behavior described in the domain rules.

Confirm the live seller profile may have changed since the snapshot was created, but the snapshot response still reflects the historical state rather than current profile data. Also confirm no mutable live-profile fields are exposed in the snapshot payload.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because this endpoint is administrator-scoped.

functions.name: test_api_seller_profile_snapshot_retrieve_history

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can retrieve a preserved seller profile snapshot by sellerProfileId and snapshotId, and that the response returns the immutable historical storefront state for dispute review even after the live seller profile has been edited. Use an existing seller profile with at least one snapshot, then request that preserved snapshot and assert the returned data reflects the historical shop name, description, and logo values captured at that snapshot time. The scenario should confirm that snapshot retrieval is independent of later live-profile changes and that the snapshot remains accessible to administrators as read-only historical data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because seller profile snapshot retrieval requires administrator access.

functions.name: test_api_seller_profile_snapshot_access_after_profile_change

scenario.draft: Verify scope protection when the snapshot identifier does not belong to the sellerProfileId in the request. Request a snapshot using a valid seller profile identifier paired with a snapshot from a different seller profile, and confirm the API responds with not found rather than exposing cross-profile historical data. Also verify the same not-found behavior when the seller profile itself does not exist. This ensures the endpoint only resolves snapshots within the correct storefront history and does not leak records across sellers.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because the endpoint is restricted to administrator review access.

functions.name: test_api_seller_profile_snapshot_scope_mismatch_not_found

scenario.draft: Verify that a category browsing request returns only active marketplace categories in a paginated response, with the current page metadata and a lightweight summary list. Cover the main browsing flow by requesting top-level categories with a page and limit, then assert that each returned item includes the category identity, name, description, timestamps, and immediate parent reference when applicable. Validate that deleted categories are excluded from the browsing surface and that the response remains usable for both customer browsing and administrative category management screens. Also confirm the endpoint returns an empty page rather than an error when no active categories match the requested slice.

functions.name: test_api_category_browse_pagination

scenario.draft: Test category browsing with the optional parent-category filter to ensure the hierarchy is exposed correctly. Request categories for a specific parent category identifier and confirm that only direct subcategories under that parent are returned, while top-level categories are excluded from that filtered view. Then repeat the browse with a null parent filter to confirm that only top-level categories are surfaced. This scenario should validate that the browsing structure supports the marketplace’s one-level subcategory navigation and that category lists reflect the expected parent-child organization used on customer category pages.

functions.name: test_api_category_browse_parent_filter

scenario.draft: Validate keyword-based browsing by searching categories using text that matches either the category name or description. Confirm that matching categories are returned in a paginated list and that unrelated categories are omitted. Include a follow-up check that a search with no matching categories returns an empty result page with valid pagination metadata. This scenario focuses on the business browsing behavior that helps customers and administrators find categories by label or description without exposing deleted categories or requiring any category-management privileges.

functions.name: test_api_category_browse_keyword_search

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can retrieve a top-level category by its UUID and receive the full category detail payload. Assert that the response includes the category id, name, description, timestamps, and a null parent when the category has no parent. Also confirm the endpoint is read-only and returns the same category data needed for category browsing without exposing children or mutating state. Include a negative check that a deleted category is not returned as an active category and is treated as not found for active browsing flows.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because category browsing is available to authenticated shoppers.

functions.name: test_api_category_retrieve_top_level_detail

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can retrieve a subcategory and that the response preserves the immediate parent relationship. Assert that the returned parent object contains only the direct parent category summary data and that the response does not attempt to expand beyond one level of hierarchy. This should validate the customer-facing browsing structure for nested categories and confirm the category detail is suitable for navigation from the category list into a specific subcategory page.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because category browsing is available to authenticated shoppers.

functions.name: test_api_category_retrieve_subcategory_with_parent

scenario.draft: Verify that requesting a category that has been deleted or is otherwise no longer active is handled as a business-level not-found outcome, and that such categories do not appear in normal customer browsing flows. The test should confirm that the category detail endpoint does not expose removed marketplace categories and that stale links or obsolete category identifiers are rejected from active navigation. This scenario validates category detail behavior for customers encountering a category that has been removed from the catalog.

functions.name: test_api_category_retrieve_deleted_or_missing_category

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can create a top-level marketplace category successfully. The test should confirm the request is authorized by an administrator session, the category is created without needing any parent category linkage, and the response returns the newly created category data needed for browsing and product organization. Also verify that the created category can be used as a normal top-level category in later catalog management flows.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because this endpoint is administrator-only.

functions.name: test_api_category_create_top_level_category

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can create a direct subcategory under an existing top-level category, and that the new category is linked only one level deep. The test should first use the category browsing endpoint to identify or confirm an existing top-level parent category, then create a child category referencing that parent, and confirm the response contains the child category with the expected parent relationship. Validate that the subcategory is accepted as a normal catalog category and remains immediately available for product assignment and category browsing. This scenario should focus on the supported one-level nesting rule and ensure the new category is created only when the parent is a valid top-level category.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because category creation is restricted to administrators.
Browse categories to select a valid existing top-level category to use as the parent for subcategory creation.

functions.name: test_api_category_create_direct_subcategory

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can update an existing category's display name and description while preserving the category identity and hierarchy rules. Start by signing in as an administrator, then update a real category with a new name and description, and confirm the response returns the same category id with the revised metadata while the parent relationship remains unchanged. Also confirm that the updated category is reflected in subsequent category detail or browsing views so customer-facing and admin-facing category lists use the latest approved metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because category maintenance is restricted to admin users only.

functions.name: test_api_category_update_metadata

scenario.draft: Verify that category updates remain limited to editable metadata and do not alter category identity or create an unintended hierarchy change. Authenticate as an administrator, then update an existing top-level category with both a new name and a new description. Assert that the same category id is returned, the parent relationship is unchanged, and no deeper nesting or structural change is introduced by the update. This scenario should confirm the endpoint behaves as a controlled category-maintenance action rather than a category re-parenting or restructuring workflow.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because only administrators can modify categories.

functions.name: test_api_category_update_preserve_hierarchy

scenario.draft: Verify that category maintenance is protected from unauthorized actors and only succeeds for administrators. Create authenticated customer and seller contexts through their own join flows, then attempt to update an existing category from each non-admin role and confirm the platform rejects the request as forbidden without changing the category. Finally, perform the same update as an administrator to confirm the operation succeeds for the proper role. This scenario validates the business rule that category structure is centrally controlled and cannot be modified by customers or sellers.

functions.name: test_api_category_deletion_forbidden_for_non_administrator

scenario.draft: Verify the public product catalog search flow returns active products with correct browsing metadata. Use a mix of products across different sellers and categories, including at least one product with multiple variants and different pricing, one product with a single in-stock variant, and one soft-deleted or otherwise inactive product. Submit a search request with a keyword, category filter, price range, in-stock-only enabled, and a supported sort order. Assert that only active products matching all filters are returned, the response is paginated, and each summary includes the product identity, seller shop name, optional category summary, timestamps, and no detailed variant breakdown or review text. Confirm that in-stock-only excludes products with no purchasable variant stock, and that price filtering respects catalog-visible pricing rather than raw variant detail fields.

functions.name: test_api_product_catalog_search_browsing

scenario.draft: Verify public product browsing returns only active catalog entries and correctly reflects product availability. Seed the catalog with a mix of products: one active product with at least one purchasable in-stock variant, one product that has no variants and should appear as unavailable, and one product that is not visible in the public catalog due to its lifecycle state. Search with broad criteria that would otherwise match all three items. Assert that the active product is returned, that the no-variant product is treated as unavailable rather than purchasable, and that the non-public product does not appear in the browsing result set. Repeat with in-stock-only criteria to confirm that only products with at least one available variant remain visible. Also verify that the response preserves normal pagination metadata and that the browse result does not expose snapshot history or detailed internal state beyond the public listing view.

functions.name: test_api_product_catalog_active_listing_visibility

scenario.draft: Verify that the product detail endpoint returns the customer-facing payload for an active product and that the response includes the full structure needed for browsing: product identity, name, description, base price, seller summary, category summary or null when uncategorized, complete image list, complete variant list, and lifecycle timestamps. Confirm that the seller and category are populated consistently with the product’s current active state, and that the returned images and variants reflect the product’s current listing rather than historical snapshots. Also verify that the endpoint can be used after a seller has updated profile information or product metadata by checking that the latest active values are returned. The response should be suitable for product detail rendering and should not apply unrelated list/search shaping.

functions.name: test_api_product_detail_retrieve_active_listing

scenario.draft: Verify that a viewer can request a product that exists but is not currently available to shoppers due to platform state, and that the endpoint responds with the appropriate not-found or access-related result rather than exposing the hidden product. Cover an unavailable listing scenario such as a deleted product or a product that is no longer visible in the customer-facing catalog. The test should ensure the detail endpoint does not leak stale product data when the product is no longer meant to be browsed, while still allowing the platform to distinguish a valid product identifier from an accessible storefront listing. If the product is visible to administrators but not customers, confirm customer-facing access is blocked while preserving the business rule that only visible products are returned for shopper detail views.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because this scenario validates customer-facing access to product detail visibility rules.

functions.name: test_api_product_detail_hidden_listing_access

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated seller can create a new product listing with the required public product data and optional category context, and that the response returns a product owned by the caller with the expected seller association. The test should confirm the product is persisted as a standalone listing record for catalog use, while images and variants are not part of this creation step.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller before creating the product listing.

functions.name: test_api_seller_product_creation

scenario.draft: Verify that product creation works when the seller assigns an eligible category, including a subcategory, and that the created product is returned with the category reflected in its detail context. The scenario should ensure the created listing belongs to the authenticated seller, uses the submitted name, description, and base price, and is accepted only when the referenced category exists and is valid for assignment. This test focuses on the normal catalog-organization workflow where a seller publishes a product into the marketplace taxonomy.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller before creating the product listing.

functions.name: test_api_seller_product_creation_with_category

scenario.draft: Verify that product creation is rejected at the business level when the caller is not a seller authorized to manage products, even if the request payload is otherwise shaped correctly. The test should demonstrate that only the authenticated seller actor can create marketplace products and that unauthorized access does not result in a new product record being persisted. This protects product ownership boundaries and ensures only seller accounts can introduce new catalog listings.

Then request the order-item detail endpoint using the orderId of one order and the orderItemId that belongs to the other order to verify the API enforces strict order-scoped ownership. The expected business behavior is that the endpoint must not return an item from a different order, preventing cross-order data leakage. Also verify the normal success path by requesting the same endpoint with the matching orderId and orderItemId pair for the legitimate order item.

The scenario should assert that preserved purchase data remains protected from cross-account access while legitimate access remains available to the owner. If the implementation returns a forbidden or not-found response for the second customer, that is acceptable; the key outcome is that the item is not returned to the wrong account.

Verify the second submission is rejected by business rules and that the original active cancellation request remains unchanged. scenario.draft: Verify that the endpoint preserves inventory history integrity when a stock movement would violate business rules for the target variant. Use an existing variant whose stock state would make the requested delta unacceptable, such as a movement that would push the stock below the allowed limit or target a variant that is not accessible to the administrator context. Assert that the operation does not create a history record, does not change the variant's current stock, and leaves the existing inventory trail untouched. This scenario focuses on the business outcome and atomic rollback behavior rather than field validation: the system must reject the movement as a stock-management failure and preserve the audit trail exactly as it was before the call.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because the inventory history endpoint is available only to administrators.

functions.name: test_api_inventory_records_stock_safeguard

scenario.draft:
Verify that the owning seller can retrieve one inventory history entry for a product variant and that the response exposes the exact historical record, not a computed stock summary. The scenario should authenticate as the seller owner, use a variant and inventory record that belong together, and confirm the response includes the record ID, the nested product variant summary, the signed quantity change, the reason, and the occurrence/creation/update timestamps. Validate that the returned record matches the requested variant scope and that the endpoint does not alter inventory state or current stock.

Also confirm the endpoint behaves as a pure read by checking the inventory history entry is unchanged before and after the request. This scenario should focus on the normal seller ownership path and the integrity of the historical payload.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the owning seller before accessing seller-scoped inventory history.

functions.name: test_api_inventory_record_retrieve_by_owner

scenario.draft:
Verify that an administrator can retrieve a specific inventory history entry for any product variant and see the same immutable history payload expected for governance review. Authenticate as an administrator, then request an inventory record for a known variant and confirm the response returns the full inventory record with its nested product variant summary, signed quantity change, reason, and timestamps. The test should ensure the administrator path is accepted even though the record is seller-owned, and that the read response remains immutable and does not change current stock or history.

This scenario should also confirm the endpoint can be used for audit tracing: the exact record requested is returned, and the payload is suitable for reviewing a historical stock movement.

scenario.draft: Verify that the snapshot image collection can be replaced in a single atomic update for the owning seller. Start with a seller who owns the product and a product snapshot that already has multiple preserved images. Submit a full ordered image list using only images that belong to that same snapshot. Confirm the API returns the updated snapshot image collection in the exact order supplied, with the first image preserved as the thumbnail order, and that the snapshot remains tied to the same product. Also confirm that this operation affects only the historical snapshot image records and does not change the live product image set. As a secondary check, verify that the update remains stable when the request reorders the same valid snapshot images rather than changing membership.

functions.name: test_api_product_snapshot_images_update_order

scenario.draft: Verify membership and product-scope enforcement for snapshot image updates. Use an authenticated seller and target a product snapshot, then submit an image list that includes an image from a different product or an image that is not part of the selected snapshot. The request should be rejected as a whole, with no partial reorder or partial membership change applied. After the failed update, confirm the preserved snapshot image order is unchanged and the historical record still reflects the original gallery state. This scenario should also cover the case where the productId and snapshotId do not describe the same snapshot context, ensuring the endpoint does not allow cross-product snapshot mutation.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the product-owning seller before attempting an update that should be rejected on business-rule grounds.

functions.name: test_api_product_snapshot_images_reject_foreign_membership

scenario.draft: Verify that only the owning seller can modify a product snapshot’s preserved image order. Authenticate as a seller who does not own the target product and attempt to update the snapshot image collection for that product. The platform should deny the operation based on ownership rules, leaving the snapshot unchanged. Confirm the failure occurs before any image records are modified, and that the product snapshot continues to be readable in its prior preserved form. This scenario is important because the endpoint works on historical product data that must remain protected from cross-seller edits, while still allowing the product owner to manage presentation history.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a different seller account to exercise cross-owner access control.

functions.name: test_api_product_snapshot_images_reject_non_owner_access

scenario.draft: As an authenticated administrator, verify that the snapshot image update operation is isolated to the product context in the URL path. Using pre-existing fixture data where the provided snapshot ID belongs to a different product than the path product ID, confirm the API rejects the cross-product rewrite attempt and preserves the original snapshot image set. Also verify the same endpoint succeeds when the snapshot ID and product ID refer to the same product context, so the scenario covers both the protected mismatch case and the normal authorized case.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because this endpoint requires administrator privileges.

functions.name: test_api_product_snapshot_images_product_scope_protection

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated seller can retrieve one preserved image record from a product snapshot that belongs to their own product. Use a product that has at least one historical snapshot with multiple images preserved in a defined order. Confirm the response returns the exact stored snapshot-image fields: id, shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id, image_uri, display_order, and created_at, and that the returned image belongs to the requested snapshot for the requested product. Also verify the historical record remains accessible even if the live product has since been edited or deleted, as long as the snapshot and image still exist. This scenario should validate the business rule that snapshot-time gallery order and image URI are preserved for audit and dispute review.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the owning seller so the snapshot history can be accessed under the correct actor boundary.

functions.name: test_api_product_snapshot_image_retrieve_own_history

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can retrieve a preserved image entry from any product snapshot and receive the immutable historical data exactly as stored. Validate that the response includes the stored image URI and display order from the snapshot history, not the current live product image order, and that deleted live products remain readable through preserved snapshot records. This scenario confirms administrator audit access to historical product presentation data for governance and dispute resolution.

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can retrieve their preserved order history as a paginated, newest-first list. Prepare a customer session, ensure the customer has multiple completed orders across different dates, then call the endpoint with a typical page and limit. Assert that the response contains only the authenticated customer's orders, that the newest order appears first, and that each summary exposes the expected order-list fields only: order number, order date, total price, and overall order status. Also verify pagination metadata is consistent with the returned slice. Include a business check that order history is built from preserved order records rather than active profile data by confirming the same history remains available even if the customer profile has been removed from active customer views.

functions.name: test_api_customer_order_history_list

scenario.draft: Verify that order history still resolves correctly after the customer account has been deleted, because historical purchases must remain preserved for legal and seller-record purposes. Set up a customer with at least one prior order, then remove the active account state through the account-deletion workflow, and finally call the order-history endpoint using the same preserved identity context available to the test harness. Assert that previously placed orders are still returned, that they remain in the history list rather than disappearing with the account, and that the list contents are still based on preserved order records. Confirm the endpoint does not fail simply because the active customer profile no longer exists, and that the order list remains sorted newest first.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the customer who originally owns the order history so the test can establish preserved purchase records before the account is removed.

Authenticate a customer account that has never placed an order, then call the endpoint with standard pagination parameters. Assert that the response is a valid empty page with zero records and zero returned items rather than an error. As a complementary ownership check, use another customer account that does have historical orders and confirm those orders are not exposed to the no-order customer session; the endpoint must only return orders belonging to the currently authenticated customer and never cross-account data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because the endpoint returns history only for the currently logged-in shopper.

Call the endpoint with that orderId and assert the response returns the preserved tracking information for the order, including one entry per shipment and shipment-level tracking details that remain stable as part of the historical order record. Also verify that the endpoint does not expose unrelated item mutation data and that the tracking view is still retrievable even after later catalog or profile changes unrelated to the order.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the customer who owns the order before accessing customer-only order tracking.

functions.name: test_api_customer_order_tracking_success

Prepare a customer-owned order that exists but has not been shipped, then call the endpoint and confirm the response does not invent shipment entries, carrier details, or tracking numbers. The scenario should validate that the API cleanly represents the absence of shipment tracking while still treating the order as viewable to its owner.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the order owner before checking shipment tracking.
Create or prepare a customer-owned order that exists without any shipment records yet.

functions.name: test_api_customer_order_tracking_not_yet_shipped

scenario.draft: Verify that the endpoint enforces order ownership and does not expose shipment tracking to another customer. Prepare two customer accounts, create an order for the first customer with shipment tracking information, then authenticate as the second customer and request the first customer's orderId. Assert the request is rejected according to the platform's access-control behavior and that no shipment carrier or tracking details are returned. This scenario protects the preserved purchase record from unauthorized access while still allowing the legitimate owner to view tracking data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate the customer whose order will be used as the protected target record.
Create or prepare a customer-owned order that contains shipment tracking data for the protected record.
Authenticate a different customer to verify unauthorized access is blocked.

Verify the response reflects the updated order aggregate after enforcement, including cancelled order items, restored inventory for the affected quantities, and the correct final order status. Also confirm that preserved purchase history remains intact in the returned representation, including customer context, shipping address, order items, and shipment context, so the operation changes current operational state without destroying auditable order records.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator so the privileged force-cancel endpoint can be accessed.

functions.name: test_api_order_force_cancel_success

Verify the operation does not apply a second cancellation, the persisted order state remains unchanged, and no additional inventory restoration or status mutation occurs. The key assertion is that duplicate administrative intervention on a finalized order is blocked while the original final state is preserved.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator so the privileged force-cancel endpoint can be accessed.

functions.name: test_api_order_force_cancel_already_finalized

This scenario validates the administrative access boundary for forced order cancellation without testing input validation behavior.

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform

I want to create an e-commerce shopping mall platform.

## Customer Account

- This platform requires registration to use any features (no guest browsing)
- Customers sign up with email and password
- Customers log in with email and password
- Customers can change their password
- Customers can delete their account
- When a customer deletes their account:
  - Their profile information is deleted
  - Their orders and order history are preserved (for seller records and legal purposes)
  - Their reviews are preserved but shown as "deleted user"

## Customer Profile

- Each customer has a profile with: display name and phone number
- Customers can edit their display name and phone number

## Address Management

- Customers can add multiple shipping addresses
- Each address has: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country
- Customers can edit their addresses
- Customers can delete their addresses
- Customers can set one address as the default shipping address

## Seller Account

- Sellers sign up with email and password
- Sellers log in with email and password
- Sellers can change their password
- Seller accounts require administrator approval before they can sell
- Sellers can view their approval status (pending, approved, rejected)
- If rejected, sellers can view the rejection reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Sellers can delete their account only if:
  - They have no pending orders (paid or shipped status)
  - They have no pending cancellation or refund requests
- When a seller deletes their account:
  - Their products are deleted from listings
  - Order history and snapshots are preserved
  - Their shop name in past orders is preserved

## Seller Profile

- Each seller has a profile with: shop name, shop description, and logo image
- Sellers can edit their shop name, description, and logo
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can view seller profiles

## Categories

- Products are organized into categories
- Categories can have subcategories (one level of nesting only)
- Each category has: name and description
- Categories are created and managed by administrators only
- Customers can browse the list of all categories
- Customers can view products within a category

## Snapshot Principle

- This is a platform where money is exchanged, so all data modifications must be recorded
- Whenever editable data is modified, a snapshot is created to preserve the previous state
- Snapshots record: when the change was made, what was changed, and the values before and after
- Snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted
- Snapshots can be viewed by relevant parties (owners, administrators) for dispute resolution

**Product Snapshot Structure**
- When a product is edited, a product snapshot is created
- The product snapshot includes all product fields (name, description, category, base price, images)
- The product snapshot also includes snapshots of all variants at that moment (product-snapshot → product-snapshot-SKU)
- This preserves the complete state of a product and its variants at any point in time

**Snapshot applies to:**
- Products (all fields including images)
- Product variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Seller profiles (shop name, description, logo)
- Order items (product, variant, and seller profile at time of purchase)
- Reviews (rating, text content)
- Cancellation requests (reason, status changes)
- Refund requests (reason, status changes)

## Products

- Sellers can create products
- Every product has:
  - Name (required)
  - Description (required)
  - Category (required, can select a subcategory)
  - Base price (required)
- Products belong to the seller who created them
- Sellers can edit their own products
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete their own products only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for any variant of the product
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for any variant of the product
- Deleting a product also deletes all its variants and inventory records
- Deleted products no longer appear in search or category listings
- Sellers can view snapshots of their own products
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Snapshots are preserved even after product deletion

## Product Images

- Sellers can upload multiple images for each product
- Images can be reordered (first image is the main/thumbnail image)
- Sellers can delete images from their products
- Image changes are included in product snapshots

## Product Variants (SKU)

- A product can have multiple variants
- Each variant represents a specific combination of options (e.g., "Red / Large", "Blue / Small")
- Each variant has:
  - SKU code (unique identifier, required)
  - Option values (e.g., color: "Red", size: "Large")
  - Price (can override the base price, optional)
  - Stock quantity (required, starts at 0)
- Sellers can add variants to their products
- Sellers can edit variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Every variant edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete variants only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for that variant
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for that variant
- A product must have at least one variant to be purchasable
- Products with no variants are visible in search but shown as "unavailable"

## Inventory Management

- Each variant has its own stock quantity
- Stock quantity is managed through inventory history records (not snapshots)
- Each inventory record contains: quantity change (positive for restocking, negative for orders/adjustments), reason, and timestamp
- Current stock is calculated by summing all inventory records
- Sellers can add inventory (restock) with a quantity and reason
- Sellers can subtract inventory (adjustment/loss) with a quantity and reason
- Order placement automatically creates a negative inventory record
- Order cancellation/refund automatically creates a positive inventory record
- Sellers can view the full inventory history of each variant
- When stock reaches 0, the variant is shown as "out of stock"
- Out of stock variants cannot be added to cart

## Product Search

- Customers can search products by name
- Search results show products from all sellers
- Search results are paginated
- Customers can filter search results by:
  - Category
  - Price range (minimum and maximum)
  - In-stock only
- Customers can sort search results by:
  - Newest first
  - Price (low to high)
  - Price (high to low)

## Product Listing

- When viewing a list of products (search results, category page), each product shows:
  - Main image (thumbnail)
  - Name
  - Base price (or price range if variants have different prices)
  - Seller shop name
  - Average rating (if reviews exist)

## Product Detail Page

- Customers can view a single product's full details
- The page shows:
  - All images
  - Name and description
  - Category
  - Seller shop name (links to seller profile)
  - All available variants with prices and stock status
  - Average rating and total review count
  - All reviews

## Wishlist

- Customers can add products to their wishlist
- Customers can view their wishlist
- The wishlist is paginated
- Wishlist shows products (not specific variants)
- Customers can remove products from their wishlist
- If a product is deleted by the seller, it is automatically removed from all wishlists

## Shopping Cart

- Customers can add variants to their cart (must select a specific variant, not just a product)
- When adding to cart, customers specify the quantity
- If the same variant is already in the cart, the quantities are combined (not added as a separate line)
- Customers can view their cart
- Cart shows each item with: product name, variant options, price, quantity, and subtotal
- Customers can change the quantity of items in their cart
- Customers can remove items from their cart
- Cart shows the total price of all items
- If a variant's stock is less than the cart quantity, a warning is shown
- If a variant is deleted or out of stock, it is marked as unavailable in the cart

## Checkout

- Customers can proceed to checkout from their cart
- Unavailable items cannot be checked out
- Customers must select a shipping address (or use default)
- Customers can review the order summary before placing the order:
  - List of items with prices
  - Shipping address
  - Total price
- Once an order is placed, the shipping address cannot be changed

## Payment

- After reviewing, customers confirm and place the order
- Payment is processed (assume external payment gateway integration)
- Payment can succeed or fail
- If payment fails, the order is not created and customers can retry
- If payment succeeds, the order is created

## Order Creation

- When an order is placed successfully:
  - Stock quantities are decreased for each purchased variant
  - Items are removed from the customer's cart
  - An order record is created
  - Each purchased variant becomes an order item with status "paid"
  - A snapshot of each purchased product and variant is saved with the order item (preserves product name, description, variant options, and price at the time of purchase)
  - A snapshot of each seller's profile is saved with the order item (preserves shop name and logo at the time of purchase)

## Order Structure

- An order contains one or more order items
- Each order item represents a purchased product variant with a quantity
- If a customer buys 3 of the same variant, it becomes one order item with quantity 3
- Order items can be from different sellers
- Each order item has its own status
- Each order item can be individually cancelled or refunded
- Order items are grouped into shipments when shipped (see Shipping and Tracking)

## Order History

- Customers can view a list of all their orders
- The list is paginated and sorted by newest first
- Each order in the list shows: order number, date, total price, and overall order status
- Customers can view the full details of an order:
  - List of items with: product name, variant, quantity, price, and item status
  - Shipping address
  - List of shipments with tracking information (each shipment shows which items are included)

## Order Status

**Order Item Status**
- Each item in an order has its own status
- Item statuses:
  - Paid: payment completed, waiting for seller to ship
  - Shipped: seller has shipped the item
  - Delivered: item has been delivered
  - Cancelled: item was cancelled
  - Refunded: item was refunded

**Order Status**
- The overall order status is derived from its items
- If all items are paid → order is "paid"
- If any item is shipped (and none delivered yet) → order is "shipped"
- If all items are delivered → order is "delivered"
- If all items are cancelled → order is "cancelled"
- If all items are refunded → order is "refunded"
- Mixed states (e.g., some delivered, some refunded) → order is "partially completed"

## Shipping and Tracking

**Shipment Concept**
- A shipment is a package sent by a seller
- A shipment can contain one or more order items from the same seller
- Different sellers always ship separately (different shipments)
- A seller can choose to ship items individually or bundle multiple items into one shipment

**Shipping Process**
- Sellers can view order items for their products that need shipping
- When shipping, sellers select one or more of their items to include in a shipment
- Sellers enter tracking information for the shipment (carrier name, tracking number)
- All items in the same shipment share the same tracking information
- When a shipment is created, all items in it change to status "shipped"

**Delivery Confirmation**
- Customers can view tracking information for each shipment
- Customers confirm delivery per shipment (not per item)
- When the customer confirms delivery, all items in that shipment change to status "delivered"
- If the customer does not confirm, items automatically change to "delivered" after 14 days from shipping

## Order Cancellation

- Cancellation is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request cancellation for individual items with status "paid" (not yet shipped)
- Cancellation requests include a reason (text)
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the cancellation request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is cancelled and refund is processed for that item only
- Cancelled items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order continue processing normally
- If all items in an order are cancelled, the entire order status becomes "cancelled"

## Refund Requests

- Refund is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request a refund for individual items with status "delivered"
- Refund requests include a reason (text)
- Refund can be requested within 7 days of that item being delivered
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the refund request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is refunded
- Refunded items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order are unaffected
- If all items in an order are refunded, the entire order status becomes "refunded"

## Reviews and Ratings

- Customers can write a review for products they have purchased
- A review can only be written after that item's status is "delivered"
- Customers can write one review per product per order
- Each review has:
  - Rating (1 to 5 stars, required)
  - Text content (optional)
- Reviews are displayed on the product detail page
- Reviews are sorted by newest first
- Customers can edit their own reviews
- Every review edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can delete their own reviews (but snapshots are preserved)
- Product's average rating is calculated from all non-deleted reviews

## Seller Dashboard

- Sellers can view a summary of their shop:
  - Total number of products
  - Total number of order items (for their products)
  - Number of pending cancellation requests
  - Number of pending refund requests
- Sellers can view a list of all order items for their products
- Sellers can filter order items by status

## Administrator System

**Becoming an Administrator**
- Any user (customer or seller) can submit a request to become an administrator
- The request includes a reason (text)
- Super administrators can view the list of pending requests
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- When approved, the user becomes a regular administrator

**Administrator Grades**
- There are two grades: regular administrator and super administrator
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves

**Seller Management**
- Administrators can view the list of pending seller approvals
- Administrators can approve or reject seller registrations
- When rejecting, administrators must provide a reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Administrators can suspend seller accounts
- When a seller is suspended:
  - Their products are hidden from search and category listings
  - Their products cannot be purchased
  - They can still process existing orders (ship items, respond to cancellation/refund requests)
  - They cannot create new products or edit existing products
- Administrators can unsuspend seller accounts (products become visible again)

**Category Management**
- Administrators can create categories and subcategories
- Administrators can edit category names and descriptions
- Administrators can delete categories (products in deleted categories become uncategorized)

**Product Oversight**
- Administrators can view all products on the platform
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Administrators can delete any product (for policy violations)

**Order Oversight**
- Administrators can view all orders on the platform
- Administrators can force-cancel individual items or entire orders (refunds the customer, restores stock)
- Administrators can force-refund individual items or entire orders

**User Management**
- Administrators can view all customer accounts
- Administrators can ban customers (banned customers cannot log in)
- Administrators can unban customers
- Administrators can view all seller accounts
- Administrators can ban sellers (banned sellers cannot log in, existing orders remain)
